title: Slipway Agents Configuration
description: Model configuration for slipway-agents pipeline. Edit this file to assign models per agent and per category. The slipway-agents plugin reads this file at OpenCode startup and enforces the assignments at runtime.

agents.description: Model assignments per agent. Keys must match agent names exactly.

categories.description: Fallback model pools by category. Used when an agent has no explicit model or when its primary model is unavailable.

quick.description: Fast, cheap models for pattern-matching and trivial tasks.

standard.description: Default for most generation and analysis tasks.

deep.description: Reasoning-heavy tasks — validation, security audit, orchestration.

agentConfig.description: Model configuration for a single agent.

model.description: Primary model string in provider/model-id format. Example: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5

fallback_model.description: Model to use if the primary model is unavailable. Uses the same provider/model-id format. If omitted, falls back to the category default.

mode.description: OpenCode agent mode. primary = appears in @ picker as main agent. subagent = invoked by orchestrator only.

description.description: Human-readable note about this agent's role. Not used at runtime.

category.description: Which category pool (from top-level `categories`) this agent falls back to if it has no model set, or if its model/fallback_model are both unavailable at runtime.

prompt_append.description: Additional system prompt text appended after the bundled agent prompt. It never replaces the base prompt.

permission.description: Scoped permissions for this agent. Absence of a key means no access to that action at all — this is NOT the same as setting it to 'deny' explicitly, though both result in no access. Most agents should have no permission block at all (doc-only agents never touch bash).

webfetch.description: Only the flat string form ("ask", "allow", "deny") is runtime-safe for webfetch. The object form is present for schema-compatibility only — it passes this repo's Zod validation but crashes OpenCode's native TUI runtime, which expects PermissionActionConfig | undefined for webfetch.

skill.description: Skill permissions must be deny-default allow-lists. Keep the object form flexible for per-pattern ask/allow/deny entries, but do not set "*" to "allow" for skill because that permits harness-default or external skills to bypass Slipway mode gates. Use "*": "deny" plus explicit repo-local skill names that the agent legitimately invokes.

bash.description: Only agents that need shell access (currently: gunner, for vulnerability scanning) should set this. Prefer the object form to scope down to specific commands rather than blanket allow.

ralphLoopConfig.description: Retry-loop configuration for agents that run bounded optimization cycles (e.g. bosun's Critical-finding resolution loop, currently hardcoded to 2 cycles in the orchestrator). At the top level this is the global default; inside an agent entry it is a per-agent override — all fields optional, unset fields inherit the global value.

block_on_exhaustion.description: If true, and Critical findings remain after max_iterations, halt the pipeline and require explicit user decision instead of silently proceeding to the next stage.

categoryConfig.description: Model configuration for a category fallback pool.

fallback_model.description: Fallback if the category default is unavailable.

description.description: Human-readable note. Not used at runtime.
